beginner.headline: People Protest New Data Centre Plans
beginner.brief: Hundreds of people are protesting new data centre plans. They worry about the data centre's effects on the local landscape. Developers want to build a large computer complex. This project could create many jobs during construction. About 300 people came to a rally to show their opposition. More than 22,500 people signed a petition against the plan. An opponent said the centre would destroy a beautiful part of the area.

intermediate.headline: Local Residents Oppose New Data Centre Project
intermediate.brief: Hundreds of people have shown strong opposition to a proposed data centre. Opponents are concerned about its potential effects on the local area. A company wants to construct a complex on a 101-acre site in Gwynedd. The proposed site is located between Caernarfon and Y Felinheli. Canolfan Ddata Menai, the company, states the project could create more than 900 temporary construction roles and 200 permanent positions. Approximately 300 individuals gathered for a rally in Caernarfon to express their disagreement. Additionally, over 22,500 people have signed a document opposing the development. Local resident Ernest Dyson believes the project would cause "the destruction of the most beautiful part of the Menai Strait." He also stated that "The people of the area are custodians of it." Local opponent Ernest Dyson highlighted the need for appropriate regulations for such large-scale developments. He also noted Wales has a history of extractive industries that often left little benefit for communities. Canolfan Ddata Menai claims the project will have "no undue impact" on the Menai Strait.

advanced.headline: Gwynedd Residents Protest Major Data Centre Development
advanced.brief: Hundreds of people have taken part in a protest against plans to build a new data centre because of concerns about its effects on the area. Placard-waving opponents highlight concerns about a data centre development on the local landscape. Developers want to construct a complex on a 101-acre site between Caernarfon and Y Felinheli, in Gwynedd. They claim it could create more than 900 roles during construction and 200 permanent roles. About 300 gathered for a rally in Caernarfon to highlight their opposition. More than 22,500 people have signed a petition opposing the plan. Canolfan Ddata Menai has previously stated its proposals would "transform and revitalise the long-derelict" site and offer significant employment. However, local opponent Ernest Dyson said the project represented "basically the destruction of the most beautiful part of the Menai Strait". He further conveyed his incredulity, stating, "It is quite incredible it should come to this." Liz Saville Roberts, the Plaid Cymru MP for Dwyfor Meirionnydd, commented that data centres must be "the right size, the right technology and in the right places." She stressed the need for "proper regulations" and ensuring communities benefit from such developments. Roberts highlighted Wales's "too long a history of extractive industries that left nothing behind and have little benefit for communities." She asserted that this pattern "mustn't happen again in the 21st Century." Canolfan Ddata Menai responded that the project would ensure "continued use" of the surrounding area, including Lôn Las Menai cycleway and footpath. They also claimed it would have "no undue impact" on the Menai Strait and an associated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI).
